standard: ISO 26262:2018 Part 2 §6.4.11 — Safety Case (GSN structured argument)
top_level_claim: rust-MQTT v1.0.0 is sufficiently safe for use as an ASIL-B/SIL-2 Safety Element Out Of Context in vehicle MQTT communication applications, subject to the integration assumptions in SAFETY_MANUAL.md.

evidence.description: Requirements registry with bidirectional traceability
Source-code requirement annotations (//fusa:req)
FMEA with 15 entries, RPN scores, ASIL assignments
TARA with 10 threats, STRIDE, CVSS 3.1 scores
HARA with 6 hazardous events and 6 safety goals (ISO 26262 Part 3)
Boundary diagram with trust boundaries
Unit and integration tests (70+ passing)
Static analysis — cargo clippy -D warnings, zero warnings
Coding standard — cargo fmt check (ISO 26262 Part 6 §8)
RELAY spec v1.10 conformance — relay conform --strict PASS
x-FuSa full lifecycle (lint, analyze, check, trace, FMEA, TARA, HARA, qualify)
Dependency vulnerability audit — cargo audit PASS
SBOM (SPDX-2.3) covering all direct and transitive dependencies
Build provenance (SLSA level 1)
No unsafe Rust in library code
Safety manual documenting SEOOC assumptions
Tool qualification evidence (rustc TQL-4, rsfusa TQL-3, relay TQL-3)
ISO 26262 Part 6 gap report
DO-178C compatibility matrix
Cyclomatic complexity V(G) report — all functions below threshold

clauses.claim: G1: rust-MQTT correctly implements MQTT v3.1.1 message routing per §4.7
clauses.strategy: Argument by exhaustive test coverage of all §4.7 wildcard rules

clauses.claim: G1a: match_topic correctly handles single-level (+) wildcards
G1b: match_topic correctly excludes $SYS topics from bare # and + wildcards
G2: rust-MQTT is free from memory-safety vulnerabilities in library code
clauses.strategy: Argument by language-enforced memory safety (no unsafe) and static analysis

clauses.claim: G3: All identified failure modes are mitigated to ALARP
clauses.strategy: Argument by FMEA coverage: all 15 failure modes have stated mitigations and residual RPN < 60

clauses.claim: G4: All identified cybersecurity threats are mitigated
clauses.strategy: Argument by TARA coverage: all 10 threats have mitigations with residual risk low or medium

clauses.claim: G5: Every requirement is implemented and tested
clauses.strategy: Argument by bidirectional traceability: 124 reqs, all with //fusa:req annotations and test references

clauses.claim: G6: The software supply chain is audited and controlled
clauses.strategy: Argument by SBOM, build provenance, cargo audit in CI, pinned Cargo.lock

clauses.claim: G7: rust-MQTT is conformant with RELAY spec v1.10 (§20)
clauses.strategy: Argument by continuous CI gate: relay conform --strict + relay interop pass on every merge

clauses.claim: G8: The development tools are qualified for TQL-3/TQL-4 use
clauses.strategy: Argument by tool qualification documentation in SAFETY_PLAN.md

clauses.claim: G9: The hazardous events identified in the HARA are mitigated by design or documented as integration obligations
clauses.strategy: Argument by HARA traceability: all 6 HEs mapped to requirements or safety manual obligations

clauses.claim: G10: ISO 26262 Part 6 coding guidelines are followed (no dead code, no complexity violations)
clauses.strategy: Argument by static analysis CI gate and cyclomatic complexity report

residual_risks: ASIL-D hazardous events (HE-001, HE-003) are integration obligations — documented in SAFETY_MANUAL.md §3,§4
THREAT-007 supply-chain residual risk is MEDIUM — mitigated by cargo audit but cannot eliminate all upstream vulnerabilities
Embedded broker (E-05) is QM, not safety-relevant; must not be deployed in vehicle
TLS is optional; integrators in network-hostile environments MUST enable the tls feature
